page: Microsoft Azure E4s_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the ESv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8171M processor cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The processor is equipped with a 35 MB L3 cache and supports AVX and AVX-512 instruction sets. Local storage consists of a 66 GB temporary disk, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates that the E4s_v3 exhibits lower-tier compute and memory performance. In stress-ng and PassMark CPU testing, the server scores in the bottom 25%, reflecting its older hardware generation. Memory bandwidth tests show read speeds of 21.57 GB/sec for large blocks and write speeds of 18.11 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 10% to 25% of tested instances. Single-threaded tasks, such as gzip compression and Geekbench single-core workloads, also fall into the bottom 10%. Redis SET operations reach 2.53 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is measured at 2.83 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E4s_v3 provides a dense memory allocation without the premium pricing of newer hardware generations, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not demand high CPU throughput. It is suitable for small to medium database deployments, caching layers, and enterprise applications requiring high memory capacity relative to compute resources. However, it is less suited for CPU-intensive tasks, high-throughput data processing, or modern LLM inference due to its constrained processing power and memory bandwidth.
